name: Reinforcement learning

subjectOf.text: Explainable reinforcement learning research has not yet produced usable explanations: the field relies on toy examples, omits user testing, produces explanations that are themselves complex, uses basic visualizations, and rarely open sources its code.
subjectOf.abstract: Current research in explainable RL, which aims to make RL models more transparent and interpretable, also has limitations. These include the use of "toy examples", lack of user testing, complexity of explanations, basic visualizations, and lack of open-sourced code.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How AI Models are Optimized Through Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4855607
scope_conditions: current explainable RL research as surveyed in the text

subjectOf.text: Deep reinforcement learning demands large amounts of training data, which suggests its algorithms differ fundamentally from human learning, and learning without supervision becomes particularly hard when rewards are sparse, as they typically are in sequence generation tasks.
subjectOf.abstract: Deep RL methods often demand large amounts of training data, suggesting that the algorithms may differ fundamentally from those underlying human learning. Moreover, learning without supervision is particularly hard when the reward is sparse, which is likely to happen for sequence generation tasks.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How AI Models are Optimized Through Web3 Governance (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4855607

subjectOf.text: The paper follows on from the author's Reinforcement Learning from Reputation Feedback paper and tests one use of that mechanism, as a filter on training data, and not the mechanism as a whole.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: Scope is relative to the author's parent reputation-feedback paper.
The restriction is the paper's own statement of what it does and does not test.
